newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada slams U.S. despite Cuba sanction suspension.
newsitem.headline: Canada slams U.S. despite Cuba sanction suspension.

text.p: Canada on Friday shrugged off U.S. President Bill Clinton's suspension of key sanctions against Cuba and criticised Washington for continuing to try to influence other countries' relations with Havana.
"I think this decision is disappointing," International Trade Minister Art Eggleton told reporters.

"It continues to be unacceptable behaviour by the United States in foisting its foreign policy onto Canada and other countries, threatening Canadian business, threatening anyone who wants to do legal business with Cuba."
Clinton announced a further six-month suspension of a provision in the Helms-Burton law that would allow U.S. citizens to sue some foreign companies doing business in Cuba.
He said he would expect to continue to suspend the law as long as U.S. allies "continue their stepped-up efforts to promote a transition to democracy in Cuba."

Eggleton said: "They (the United States) should not be continuing to hold this sword over the heads of other countries, and the businesses, the legitimate business of other countries in their operations in Cuba."
Canada is one of Cuba's biggest business partners.

He said he hoped to have some word soon on whether Canada would proceed with a challenge to the U.S. law under the North American Free Trade Agreement, which groups Canada, the United States and Mexico.
He said he would consult with his cabinet colleagues and with the Mexican government on the issue.
